title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — Boolean classification and annulus conjecture

\section*{Annulus avoidance: the low-weight-subspace argument and its exact failure}

\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Shared notation.}$\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$, and $\mathbb Z,\mathbb Q,\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ denote the integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers. Any other conventions are specified locally.


Write \(\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}\) for the field with two elements, and \(w(x)=|\{j:x_j=1\}|\) for Hamming weight. For positive integers \(n\) and integers \(1\le a\le b\), define
\[A(a,b,n)=\{x\in\mathbb F_2^n:a\le w(x)\le b\},\qquad
R_A(a,b,n)=\frac1n\max\{\dim V:V\le\mathbb F_2^n,\ V\cap A(a,b,n)=\varnothing\}.\]
This definition also applies when \(b>n\). Equivalently, \(1-R_A(a,b,n)\) is the least normalized rank of a binary matrix with kernel avoiding the annulus. Thus \(R_A\) is the rate of the avoiding subspace, rather than the normalized rank of its parity-check matrix.
For fixed \(0\le\alpha<\beta\le1\), put \(a_n=\max\{1,\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\}\), \(b_n=\lfloor\beta n\rfloor\), and \(N_n=n-a_n+1\); take sufficiently large \(n\) that \(a_n\le b_n\).
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Does the asymptotic annulus identity
\[R_A(a_n,b_n,n)=\frac{a_n-1}{n}+\frac{N_n}{n}R_A(1,b_n,N_n)+o(1)\quad(n\to\infty)\]
hold for every fixed \(0\le\alpha<\beta\le1\)? Equivalently, in the usual notation suppressing integer rounding,
\[R_A(\alpha n,\beta n,n)=\alpha+(1-\alpha)R_A(1,\beta n,(1-\alpha)n)+o(1).\]
Here \(o(1)\) denotes a quantity tending to zero for the fixed pair \((\alpha,\beta)\). \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.6528}{[S2]}

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does the largest rate of a binary linear subspace avoiding a Hamming annulus asymptotically equal the rate obtained by using free coordinates below its inner radius and a code avoiding a punctured ball on the remaining coordinates?

\subsection{Sources}
\begin{description}
\item[S1] ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems, record 2800702 (AMR-027-0702). CC BY 4.0. \url{https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulamai/UnsolvedMath}.
\item[S2] Emmanuel Abbe, Noga Alon, Afonso S. Bandeira and Colin Sandon, Linear Boolean Classification, Coding and “the Critical Problem” (2015), arXiv:1401.6528, Definition 5, equations (21)–(23); Proposition 1, equation (26); Conjecture 3, equation (34). \url{https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.6528}.
\end{description}

\subsection{Verbatim supplied catalogue question}
Prove or disprove: $R_A(\alpha n,\beta n,n)=\alpha+(1-\alpha)R_A(1,\beta n,(1-\alpha)n)+o(1)$.

\section{Attempt and results}
Put $K(a,b,n)=nR_A(a,b,n)$, the maximum dimension of an avoiding subspace,
and $K_0(b,N)=K(1,b,N)$. The latter codes have no nonzero word of weight
at most $b$; if $b\ge N$, they have dimension zero. We retain the source's
integer conventions and its fixed strict inequality $\alpha<\beta$.

\paragraph{The general constructive inequality.}
Take an optimal code $C\le\mathbb F_2^{n-a+1}$ of dimension $K_0(b,n-a+1)$
and the direct sum $V=\mathbb F_2^{a-1}\oplus C$. If a vector has a nonzero
$C$ component, its weight exceeds $b$; otherwise its weight is at most
$a-1$. Hence $V$ avoids the annulus and
\[
K(a,b,n)\ge a-1+K_0(b,n-a+1).
\]
This is the standard lower construction, not the unresolved upper bound.

\paragraph{An exact upper bound when $b\ge2a-2$.}
Let $V$ be any avoiding subspace and
$L=\{v\in V:w(v)\le a-1\}$. Then $L$ is a subspace: a sum of two such
vectors has weight at most $2a-2\le b$, and avoidance forces its weight
below $a$. Write $\ell=\dim L$. Every binary subspace of dimension $\ell$
has an information set of $\ell$ coordinates on which projection is an
isomorphism. The inverse image of the all-one vector therefore has weight
at least $\ell$. Consequently $\ell\le a-1$.
Choose such an information set $I$ for $L$. The projection of $V$ onto $I$
has rank $\ell$, since $L$ already projects onto all of $\mathbb F_2^I$.
Thus the subspace $V_0$ of vectors of $V$ vanishing on $I$ has dimension
$\dim V-\ell$. Its intersection with $L$ is zero. Every nonzero member of
$V_0$ has weight at least $a$ and hence greater than $b$.
Puncturing its zero coordinates $I$ gives a code of length $n-\ell$ and
the same dimension. Shorten this code at any $a-1-\ell$ additional
coordinates: impose zeros there and then delete them. Each imposed zero
reduces dimension by at most one and deletion preserves nonzero weights.
This produces a length-$n-a+1$ code of dimension at least
$\dim V-\ell-(a-1-\ell)=\dim V-a+1$ and minimum nonzero weight exceeding
$b$. It follows that
\[
K(a,b,n)\le a-1+K_0(b,n-a+1).
\]
Together the inequalities prove equality whenever $1\le a\le b\le n$
and $b\ge2a-2$. This is a complete rederivation of the established parameter
region, not a new extension. For $\beta\ge2\alpha$, the rounding in the
definition gives $b_n\ge2a_n-2$ for all sufficiently large $n$ (also when
$\alpha=0$, for which $a_n=1$), so the asymptotic identity is exact there.

\paragraph{The attempted extension fails at its first structural step.}
Take $n=6t$, $a=4t$, $b=5t$, and let $V$ be spanned by the indicators of
the first and last $3t$ coordinates. Its nonzero weights are $3t,3t,6t$,
so it avoids $[a,b]$. The low-weight members are zero and the two basis
vectors, but their sum is not low-weight. Hence $L$ is not a subspace.
This persists at the fixed pair $(\alpha,\beta)=(2/3,5/6)$ as $t\to\infty$.
It invalidates this proof route in a genuine positive-width regime. It does
not disprove the conjecture: this example has dimension two, with vanishing
normalized rate, and is not shown extremal.

\section{Context and adversarial audit}
Abbe, Alon, Bandeira and Sandon's primary paper, arXiv:1401.6528v3, was
consulted at Proposition 1 and Conjecture 3 on 11 October 2026. The exact
parameter region above is known. The manuscript's proof is included to
locate precisely why the low-weight argument cannot cover the remaining
region. The audit checked information-set injectivity, shortening rather
than arbitrary puncturing, and rate rather than parity-check rank. Finite
width-zero exceptions do not refute a conjecture assuming fixed
$\alpha<\beta$. A subsequent exact Python 3.14.2 check enumerated all binary
subspaces in dimensions one through six using reduced row-echelon bases
(counts 2, 5, 16, 67, 374, 2825). All general constructive lower bounds and
43 applicable exact-equality cases passed. The closure example has dimension
two whereas the exact optimum at $(n,a,b)=(6,4,5)$ is three, confirming that
it is not an extremal counterexample. The local artifacts
\texttt{exact\_checks.py} and \texttt{exact\_checks.json} contain the complete
inputs, algorithm and output; no random seed or external library is needed.
These are finite checks, not independent human proof verification.
